cases.description: An ID with reserved and non-ASCII characters verifies
Canonicalization does no Unicode normalization: the same ID in NFD form is a different label
A label with field-level encryption verifies without the decryption key
Changing a signed field makes the signature invalid
Changing `kid` to another trusted key makes the signature invalid
A `kid` that isn't in the trust store is unknown-kid
An edited label re-signed with an untrusted key under a trusted `kid` is invalid
An edited label re-signed under the attacker's own `kid` is unknown-kid
A public key carried in the label is never used: only the trust store is consulted
Removing `kid` and `signature` leaves an unsigned label, so policy must require `valid`
A label without `kid` or `signature` is unsigned
A pre-1.4 `signature` without `kid` is opaque: unsigned, preserved, never verified
`kid` without `signature` is malformed
A signature that doesn't decode to 64 bytes is malformed
A padded signature is malformed
A signature whose final character has non-zero unused bits is malformed
A signature containing standard base64 characters (`+`, `/`) is malformed
A non-string signature with `kid` is malformed
A `kid` with characters outside the allowed set is malformed
A signature with S >= L (non-canonical scalar) is invalid
Label text with a duplicate member name SHOULD be malformed
Sign an encrypted URL: append `kid`, then `sig` over everything before `&sig=`
The signed bytes include the percent-encoded ID exactly as emitted
An encrypted URL signed by a trusted key verifies
A signed URL with a percent-encoded hostile ID verifies
Re-encoding the ID (lowercase hex) decrypts to the same ID but changes the signed bytes
Parameter order is part of the signed bytes; verifiers don't reorder
Changing a signed parameter makes the signature invalid
Changing `kid` to another trusted key makes the signature invalid
A `kid` that isn't in the trust store is unknown-kid
A URL re-signed under the attacker's own `kid` is unknown-kid
A URL re-signed with an untrusted key under a trusted `kid` is invalid
A URL without `kid` or `sig` is unsigned
A pre-1.4 `sig` without `kid` is opaque: unsigned, preserved, never verified
Removing `kid` and `sig` leaves an unsigned URL
`kid` without `sig` is malformed
`sig` MUST be the last parameter
`sig` MUST appear once
`kid` MUST appear once
A `sig` that doesn't decode to 64 bytes is malformed
Malformed is decided before the `kid` lookup: a truncated `sig` under an unknown `kid` is malformed
`sig` is literal base64url; percent-escapes are malformed
